findings.title: FastUnlock: Windows Narrator LockScreen Bypass 0day Vulnerability
findings.summary_md: The researcher published the FastUnlock repository on 19 November 2026, ahead of the story's first_seen. The write-up says Narrator mishandles UI in a locked-account context and that exploitation gives code execution as the lock-screen account WsiAccount, bypassing BitLocker on a Windows 11 26H2 machine with the November patch installed. It requires physical access and at least one account linked to a Microsoft account, and describes reaching File Explorer through settings and running a binary from a USB stick. The author says the technique was consistent on every machine tested and did not test Windows 10.

findings.title: Proof of Concept for FastUnlock, Windows lock screen bypass from Nightmare Eclipse
findings.summary_md: ThreatLocker Threat Intelligence reproduced FastUnlock on 19 November 2026 and confirmed that the bypass reaches the non-administrator WSIAccount without a sign-in. The test required physical access, a Microsoft account in the recovery flow, and Narrator navigation with Caps Lock and the arrow keys; the physical keyboard could not be used while navigating Narrator, so the testers used the on-screen keyboard and an external drive. ThreatLocker says a BitLocker preboot PIN mitigates the technique on a powered-off or hibernated machine because the drive must unlock before Windows starts.

findings.title: Chaotic Eclipse Releases FastUnlock, a New Windows Zero-Day Vulnerability
findings.summary_md: Security Affairs reported the FastUnlock release on 19 November 2026, describing the Narrator-driven lock-screen bypass and code execution under WsiAccount. The article names the researcher as Chaotic Eclipse, also known as INFINITE NIGHTMARE, MSNightmare and Nightmare-Eclipse, and repeats the claim of a fully encrypted Windows 11 26H2 system breached in five minutes despite November updates. It notes the need for physical access and an online-linked account, and quotes the researcher's uncertainty about Windows 10.

findings.title: Will Dormann on FastUnlock and VU#789985
findings.summary_md: Will Dormann assessed FastUnlock on 19 November 2026 as a code-free variant of the physical-access weakness described in CERT/CC VU#789985. He said Narrator focuses on off-screen windows belonging to the ephemeral WsiAccount, letting a user launch SystemSettings.exe, set Explorer to show newly connected USB storage, and run a program from that window. He argued that calling it a BitLocker bypass is misleading: with TPM-only BitLocker the disk is already decrypted when Windows prompts for credentials, and the account obtained is a medium-integrity WsiAccount.

findings.title: VU#789985 - Physical access to a computer system can be used to bypass software-based access control mechanisms
findings.summary_md: CERT/CC originally published VU#789985 on 6 March 2003 and last revised it in July 2017. The note states that an intruder with physical access can bypass software-based access controls, boot another operating system, copy or alter encrypted data, and install hardware or Trojan horses. Its recommended controls are restricting physical access to authorized personnel and encrypting data on mobile devices. The advisory frames FastUnlock's underlying condition as a long-recognized physical-access trust boundary rather than a new class of flaw.

findings.title: ZDI-21-1053 - Microsoft Windows Lock Screen Improper Access Control Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
findings.summary_md: ZDI published ZDI-21-1053 on 2 September 2021 for a Windows lock-screen authentication bypass credited to Abdelhamid Naceri, the researcher now using the FastUnlock handles. The advisory says a physically present attacker could bypass authentication without credentials and assigns CVE-2021-26431 with a CVSS score of 6.8. Its disclosure timeline records vendor notification on 30 June 2021 and coordinated release on 2 September 2021, and Microsoft issued an update. The case is a dated precedent for the same class of lock-screen access, though ZDI does not tie it to the new Narrator path.
